title: Like magnetic poles repel, and unlike poles attract
summary: The north end of a magnet repels another north end, south repels south, and north and south attract.
body: NASA Goddard says a magnetized bar has its power concentrated at two ends, called the north and south poles, because a bar hung by its middle turns a north end northward and a south end southward. The north end repels the north end of another magnet, south repels south, and north and south attract. The page also says either pole can attract iron objects such as pins and paper clips, because the iron becomes a temporary magnet. Earth's field strength in gauss is a different card and is not restated.

sources.title: Magnetic Fields
